pr.title: Prepare an iOS device test with project ios in the implement skill
pr.head: 91176124412f8a5f6b58ced579e3161a1244f18f

summary: Projector's inbox lets an agent ask the person to test a change on their phone with a request, an inbox item whose optional start action is the one thing the agent does when the person presses start, such as installing a build. The press is the person's consent to the install. Until now the implement skill said to keep the pull request a draft during such a test but gave no way to prepare it, so each session invented its own build and install.

This pull request is the second layer of a stack. The layer below, #456, adds project ios, which builds a branch or pull request of a repository's iOS app in a worktree of its own, keeps each build, installs a kept build on a named device, and copies back crash reports and logs. This layer adds a subsection to the implement skill that tells an agent how to use those commands for a test on the person's iPhone or iPad, and points the work skill's phone-check line at it. It carries out § 2.6 of the plan in docs/projects/ios/readme.md, and, as the stack's last layer, marks that project completed.

1. Push and build ahead. The agent pushes the branch and runs project ios build <number> --no-install, and posts nothing until that build succeeds. An untrusted head is refused, and the agent never adds --allow-untrusted without the person's word.
  2. Offer an install only to a reachable device. When project ios devices --json lists a device as installable, the request gets a start action naming it, and on STARTED the agent runs project ios install <number> --device <udid>.
  3. Always give the person a command. The request's steps include project ios build <number>, which the person can run on the Mac their device is plugged into.
  4. Bring crashes and logs back. The agent runs project ios crashes --device <udid> for the device the person tested on when it can reach it, and otherwise asks the person to run crashes or logs.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first review found that the subsection named the Mac as in scope while no step passes --mac. The author scoped it to an iPhone or iPad, which matches § 2.6 of the plan, and the thread is resolved.
  • Both suggestions from that review landed: the no-device case reads as a device the agent cannot reach, and crashes takes the tested device's --device <udid>.
  • This head rebases the layer onto #456's new head with every patch unchanged. Its review is clean, with one suggestion still standing: say where the after-merge iPhone check is tracked.

groups.title: The device test in the skills
groups.kicker: How an agent prepares, starts, and follows up a device test for an iOS app
intro: The new subsection, "Prepare a device test for an iOS app", sits in the implement skill's hand-over, beside the rule that keeps a pull request a draft while the person tests it. A kept build is the copy of a built app that project ios build stores per branch or pull request, so a later install of that target installs exactly what was built for it.

The order of the steps matters for consent. The agent's own build passes --no-install, so nothing reaches the person's device until they press start, and the install names the device's UDID so it cannot land on a different device connected in the meantime.

checks.text: Every command and flag the text names, build --no-install, --allow-untrusted, install --device, devices --json with its installable field, crashes, and logs, exists in add_ios_parser at this head, read in src/projector/cli.py.

files.note: The new subsection and a link to it from the draft-while-testing rule.

checks.text: The subsection covers an iPhone or iPad only. A check on the Mac would need --mac on each command, which neither these steps nor § 2.6 of the plan describe.

choose_device in src/projector/ios.py matches --device exactly by name or UDID and refuses a device that has become unreachable, so the install reaches the device the start action names, and the error the agent blocks with says why.
crashes takes --device in add_ios_parser, prints each report's path, and logs prints the file it wrote, which is the file the person is asked to share.

files.note: Points the phone-check line at the new subsection.

groups.title: Closing the plan
groups.kicker: The plan's device-test steps match the skill, and the project is marked completed
intro: A Projector plan is the project's spec under docs/projects/, and its status says whether the work is a draft, ready, in progress, or completed. The repository's rule is to mark a project completed in the pull request that carries its last code, so it is completed when that pull request merges, and to record whether it shipped.

This layer is the last of the stack, so it brings § 2.6's steps in line with the skill's wording, sets the status to completed, and adds § 8, Outcome. One acceptance criterion, a build installed and opened on a real iPhone, is still unproven. § 8 records that the person chose to run it once the stack merges, and that a problem it finds is new work on the shipped command.

files.note: The status flip, § 2.6 steps 4 and 5 reworded to match the skill, and the new § 8, Outcome.

checks.text: project show ios reports completed at this head, project check passes, and no cited section was renumbered.
§ 8 leaves the real-iPhone check to the person after the merge but does not say where it is tracked, which the finish skill asks for. The review lists that as a suggestion, not a blocker.
